# CodeHub — Browser Extension

> CodeHub is a free, privacy-first Chrome extension that automatically syncs your accepted DSA solutions from LeetCode, GeeksforGeeks, Codeforces, CodeChef & NeetCode into a single organized GitHub repository.

- Website: https://rishijain07.github.io/codehub-extension/
- Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/codehub/dgjlfbfaepcbokmgpicnngbdfckcloaf
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/rishijain07/codehub-extension
- Author: Rishi Jain (beingrishijain@gmail.com)
- Current Version: v2.2.0 (Manifest V3)
- Pricing: 100% Free & Open Ecosystem

## Overview & Value Proposition
CodeHub eliminates the manual friction of copying and committing code after solving Data Structures & Algorithms problems. It converts every accepted solution across competitive programming and interview prep platforms into a structured GitHub repository, building an automated proof-of-work portfolio for software engineering interviews.

## Supported Platforms & Sync Mechanisms
- **LeetCode**: Instant client-side DOM hook upon receiving an "Accepted" verdict. Formats code file and generates a complete `README.md` with difficulty, tags, problem description, and performance stats.
- **GeeksforGeeks (GFG)**: Instant client-side hook on accepted code submissions.
- **Codeforces**: Automatic background polling via the official public Codeforces API using your username handle. Syncs practice submissions and contest solutions.
- **CodeChef**: Instant hook on accepted submissions for contests and practice problemsets.
- **NeetCode**: Instant hook on NeetCode 150 & NeetCode 75 problem sets.

## Architecture & Privacy Model
- **Zero Intermediary Servers**: CodeHub does not use any hosted backend or cloud database. All network requests travel directly from the user's browser to the platform API and the official GitHub REST API.
- **OAuth Device Flow**: Uses GitHub's secure Device Flow (`https://github.com/login/device`). The user never enters their GitHub password into the extension.
- **Local Storage**: The GitHub OAuth token is stored strictly in `chrome.storage.local` within the user's browser sandbox and is never transmitted anywhere else.
- **Private Repositories**: Supports both public and private GitHub repositories.

## Repository Folder Structure
When CodeHub pushes code, it organizes problems into clean platform-based directories:
```
your-dsa-repo/
├── leetcode/
│   └── 0001-two-sum/
│       ├── solution.cpp (or .py, .java, .js, .ts, etc.)
│       └── README.md
├── geeksforgeeks/
│   └── bfs-traversal-of-graph/
│       ├── solution.py
│       └── README.md
├── codeforces/
│   └── 4A-watermelon/
│       ├── solution.cpp
│       └── README.md
├── codechef/
│   └── START01/
│       ├── solution.java
│       └── README.md
├── neetcode/
│   └── neetcode-150/
│       └── ...
└── stats.json
```

## Comparison with LeetHub & Alternatives
- **Multi-Platform**: LeetHub and other tools typically only support LeetCode. CodeHub unifies 5 major platforms in a single repository.
- **Manifest V3 Native**: CodeHub is built on modern Chrome Extensions Manifest V3 architecture with a service worker, ensuring long-term compatibility.
- **Active Maintenance**: Continuously updated to adapt to UI changes on competitive programming websites.

## Setup in 60 Seconds
1. Install CodeHub from the Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/codehub/dgjlfbfaepcbokmgpicnngbdfckcloaf
2. Click the CodeHub icon in your browser toolbar and select "Authenticate with GitHub".
3. Enter the one-time device code at github.com/login/device to grant repo permissions.
4. Select your target repository or let CodeHub create a clean `DSA-Solutions` repo.
5. Solve problems on any supported platform — on "Accepted", CodeHub automatically commits your solution and documentation!
